inputs.coverage: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 126.5 km effective diameter (catalog ±1.86 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. An alternative pole remains possible. No surface imagery exists; rotational phase is illustrative. The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. Hanuš2016 Table2 reports 12 dense light curves across three apparitions plus 519 sparse measurements. Both low-latitude poles remain; no imagery or unique pole is inferred.
